Consider the following triangle:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249653/assets/e03942073ddfd8672fe5c5e4bd7bc81f0dc22f8682e3a364b001c280b315e721.png)

Calculate the measure of the angle $\angle A$ to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡A=\frac{{b}^{2}+{c}^{2}-{a}^{2}}{2bc}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have

$$
a=9,\quad b=7,\quad c=12.
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡A & =\frac{{7}^{2}+{12}^{2}-{9}^{2}}{2(7)(12)} \\  & =\frac{49+144-81}{168} \\  & =\frac{112}{168} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{2}{3}) \\  & ={48.19}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

to two decimal places.
